items.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
items.summary: Reflection's first open-weight model is now available on Ollama, and free for a limited time only. Beam is designed for software engineering, reasoning, and long-running agentic tasks. Access Beam through Ollama Cloud.

items.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
items.summary: AI agents can now use Ollama's cloud models safely inside Fly.io's cloud computers.

items.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
items.summary: Ollama now supports decision models, based on TypeSafe's Jev API for fast, typed decisions. Decision models can now be run at no cost with low latency. Based on text, decision models answer yes-or-no questions, choices and scores about it, with a probability for every option.

items.title: Ollama's transparent pricing
items.summary: Ollama's Pro, Max, and Team plans now use industry-standard per-token pricing with usage included on every plan.

items.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
items.summary: Claude Desktop can now be configured to work with Ollama as a third-party gateway provider, making it possible to use open models in Claude.

items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
items.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now available on Ollama. It's a 30 billion parameter (3B active) open model built for agents that stay running, gathering context, calling tools, and working through multi-step tasks on your own hardware.

items.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
items.summary: Meta's Muse Glimmer, the first open model released by Meta Superintelligence Labs, is now available. Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the Apache 2.0 license, designed for local coding agents, and accelerated by Ollama's MLX engine with new native DFlash and image input support.

items.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
items.summary: Serving 8.9 million developers, Ollama has raised $88M from Benchmark, Theory Ventures, 8VC, Y Combinator, and many incredible angel investors.

items.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
items.summary: Gemma 4 is now significantly faster in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon via multi-token prediction (MTP), powered by MLX. Performance is now up to 90% faster when used with coding agents, as measured using the Aider polyglot benchmark.

items.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
items.summary: Ollama's MLX engine has been updated to deliver its highest performance on Apple Silicon yet. Models output higher quality responses, respond faster, and use less memory.

items.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
items.summary: Ollama 0.30 is now available with improved performance and GGUF model compatibility through llama.cpp. This augments Ollama's MLX engine on Apple silicon, bringing support to more models on a wider range of hardware.

items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
items.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra is built for high-throughput reasoning and long-running agent workflows.

items.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
items.summary: OpenJarvis v1.0 is now available: an open-source framework for building personal AI agents that run on your own hardware, with Ollama support built-in.

items.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
items.summary: Today, we're previewing the fastest way to run Ollama on Apple silicon, powered by MLX, Apple's machine learning framework.

items.title: The simplest and fastest way to setup OpenClaw
items.summary: Setup OpenClaw in under two minutes with a single Ollama command.

items.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
items.summary: Ollama now supports subagents and web search in Claude Code.

items.title: OpenClaw
items.summary: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant that connects your messaging apps to local AI coding agents, all running on your own device.

items.title: ollama launch
items.summary: ollama launch is a new command which sets up and runs coding tools like Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex with local or cloud models. No environment variables or config files needed.

items.title: Image generation (experimental)
items.summary: Generate images locally with Ollama on macOS. Windows and Linux support coming soon.

items.title: Claude Code with Anthropic API compatibility
items.summary: Ollama is now compatible with the Anthropic Messages API, making it possible to use tools like Claude Code with open models.

items.title: OpenAI Codex with Ollama
items.summary: Open models can be used with OpenAI's Codex CLI through Ollama. Codex can read, modify, and execute code in your working directory using models such as gpt-oss:20b, gpt-oss:120b, or other open-weight alternatives.

items.title: OpenAI gpt-oss-safeguard
items.summary: Ollama is partnering with OpenAI and ROOST (Robust Open Online Safety Tools) to bring the latest gpt-oss-safeguard reasoning models to users for safety classification tasks. gpt-oss-safeguard models are available in two sizes: 20B and 120B, and are permissively licensed under the Apache 2.0 license.

items.title: MiniMax M2
items.summary: MiniMax M2 is now available on Ollama's cloud. It's a model built for coding and agentic workflows.

items.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark performance
items.summary: We ran performance tests on release day firmware and an updated Ollama version to see how Ollama performs.

items.title: New coding models & integrations
items.summary: GLM-4.6 and Qwen3-coder-480B are available on Ollama’s cloud service with easy integrations to the tools you are familiar with. Qwen3-Coder-30B has been updated for faster, more reliable tool calling in Ollama’s new engine.

items.title: Qwen3-VL
items.summary: Ollama now supports Alibaba's Qwen3-VL.

items.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark
items.summary: The latest NVIDIA DGX Spark is here! Ollama has partnered with NVIDIA to ensure it runs fast and efficiently out-of-the-box.

items.title: Web search
items.summary: A new web search API is now available in Ollama. Ollama provides a generous free tier of web searches for individuals to use, and higher rate limits are available via Ollama’s cloud.

items.title: New model scheduling
items.summary: Ollama now includes a significantly improved model scheduling system, reducing crashes due to out of memory issues, maximizing GPU utilization and performance, especially on multi-GPU systems.

items.title: Cloud models
items.summary: Cloud models are now in preview, letting you run larger models with fast, datacenter-grade hardware. You can keep using your local tools while running larger models that wouldn’t fit on a personal computer.

items.title: OpenAI gpt-oss
items.summary: Ollama partners with OpenAI to bring gpt-oss to Ollama and its community.

items.title: Ollama's new app
items.summary: Ollama's new app is now available for macOS and Windows.

items.title: Secure Minions: private collaboration between Ollama and frontier models
items.summary: Secure Minions is a secure protocol built by Stanford's Hazy Research lab to allow encrypted local-remote communication.

items.title: Thinking
items.summary: Ollama now has the ability to enable or disable thinking. This gives users the flexibility to choose the model’s thinking behavior for different applications and use cases.

items.title: Streaming responses with tool calling
items.summary: Ollama now supports streaming responses with tool calling. This enables all chat applications to stream content and also call tools in real time.

items.title: Ollama's new engine for multimodal models
items.summary: Ollama now supports new multimodal models with its new engine.

items.title: Minions: where local and cloud LLMs meet
items.summary: Avanika Narayan, Dan Biderman, and Sabri Eyuboglu from Christopher Ré's Stanford Hazy Research lab, along with Avner May, Scott Linderman, James Zou, have developed a way to shift a substantial portion of LLM workloads to consumer devices by having small on-device models (such as Llama 3.2 with Ollama) collaborate with larger models in the cloud (such as GPT-4o).

items.title: Structured outputs
items.summary: Ollama now supports structured outputs making it possible to constrain a model's output to a specific format defined by a JSON schema. The Ollama Python and JavaScript libraries have been updated to support structured outputs.

items.title: Ollama Python library 0.4 with function calling improvements
items.summary: With Ollama Python library version 0.4, functions can now be provided as tools. The library now also has full typing support and new examples have been added.

items.title: Llama 3.2 Vision
items.summary: Llama 3.2 Vision 11B and 90B models are now available in Ollama.

items.title: IBM Granite 3.0 models
items.summary: Ollama partners with IBM to bring Granite 3.0 models to Ollama.

items.title: Llama 3.2 goes small and multimodal
items.summary: Ollama partners with Meta to bring Llama 3.2 to Ollama.

items.title: Reduce hallucinations with Bespoke-Minicheck
items.summary: Bespoke-Minicheck is a new grounded factuality checking model developed by Bespoke Labs that is now available in Ollama. It can fact-check responses generated by other models to detect and reduce hallucinations.

items.title: Tool support
items.summary: Ollama now supports tool calling with popular models such as Llama 3.1. This enables a model to answer a given prompt using tool(s) it knows about, making it possible for models to perform more complex tasks or interact with the outside world.

items.title: Google Gemma 2
items.summary: Gemma 2 is now available on Ollama in 3 sizes - 2B, 9B and 27B.

items.title: An entirely open-source AI code assistant inside your editor
items.summary: Continue enables you to easily create your own coding assistant directly inside Visual Studio Code and JetBrains with open-source LLMs.

items.title: Google announces Firebase Genkit with Ollama support
items.summary: At Google IO 2024, Google announced Ollama support in Firebase Genkit, a new open-source framework for developers to build, deploy and monitor production-ready AI-powered apps.

items.title: Llama 3 is not very censored
items.summary: Compared to Llama 2, Llama 3 feels much less censored. Meta has substantially lowered false refusal rates. Llama 3 will refuse less than 1/3 of the prompts previously refused by Llama 2.

items.title: Llama 3
items.summary: Llama 3 is now available to run on Ollama. This model is the next generation of Meta's state-of-the-art large language model, and is the most capable openly available LLM to date.

items.title: Embedding models
items.summary: Embedding models are available in Ollama, making it easy to generate vector embeddings for use in search and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) applications.

items.title: Ollama now supports AMD graphics cards
items.summary: Ollama now supports AMD graphics cards in preview on Windows and Linux. All the features of Ollama can now be accelerated by AMD graphics cards on Ollama for Linux and Windows.

items.title: Windows preview
items.summary: Ollama is now available on Windows in preview, making it possible to pull, run and create large language models in a new native Windows experience. Ollama on Windows includes built-in GPU acceleration, access to the full model library, and serves the Ollama API including OpenAI compatibility.

items.title: OpenAI compatibility
items.summary: Ollama now has initial compatibility with the OpenAI Chat Completions API, making it possible to use existing tooling built for OpenAI with local models via Ollama.

items.title: Vision models
items.summary: New vision models are now available: LLaVA 1.6, in 7B, 13B and 34B parameter sizes. These models support higher resolution images, improved text recognition and logical reasoning.

items.title: Python & JavaScript Libraries
items.summary: The initial versions of the Ollama Python and JavaScript libraries are now available, making it easy to integrate your Python or JavaScript, or Typescript app with Ollama in a few lines of code. Both libraries include all the features of the Ollama REST API, are familiar in design, and compatible with new and previous versions of Ollama.

items.title: Building LLM-Powered Web Apps with Client-Side Technology
items.summary: Recreate one of the most popular LangChain use-cases with open source, locally running software - a chain that performs Retrieval-Augmented Generation, or RAG for short, and allows you to “chat with your documents”

items.title: Ollama is now available as an official Docker image
items.summary: Ollama can now run with Docker Desktop on the Mac, and run inside Docker containers with GPU acceleration on Linux.

items.title: Leveraging LLMs in your Obsidian Notes
items.summary: This post walks through how you could incorporate a local LLM using Ollama in Obsidian, or potentially any note taking tool.

items.title: How to prompt Code Llama
items.summary: This guide walks through the different ways to structure prompts for Code Llama and its different variations and features including instructions, code completion and fill-in-the-middle (FIM).

items.title: Run Code Llama locally
items.summary: Meta's Code Llama is now available on Ollama to try.

items.title: Run Llama 2 uncensored locally
items.summary: This post will give some example comparisons running Llama 2 uncensored model versus its censored model.
